Tried to do my best with avoiding spoilers for later episodes in the arc, but sorry if I messed up

Aincrad is a comparably different arc of Sword Art Online. It feels different in terms of the story it tells, largely because of these first 6 episodes. The later arcs of SAO are quite linear with the storytelling, only really spending time focusing on the main plot and not allowing time to explore the game world and the people within it, which is what happens in these first 6 episodes. Maybe that's why I prefer it.

The first two episodes did a good job at setting the stage for the arc. I quite enjoyed the whole fighting scene at the end of episode 2 where it was everyone doing their best to defeat the first floor boss. The way that everyone was working together, switching out to attack the main boss and it's goons, it felt like it was from an MMO. The hatred towards the beta testers of the game, whilst it felt contrived at the meeting of the group at the beginning of episode 2, did come across as reasonable within the end of the fight where the main group turned onto Kirito after the leader ended up being killed. It's a shame that reputation didn't seem to carry on within the rest of the episodes

The remaining 4 episodes of the block covered Kirito going out on his own and doing his own thing (dragging Asuna along for the 5th and 6th episode). Whilst it is disappointing that they don't send more time with the main group, there was something I liked about focusing on the different stories in the world. Episode 3 had Kirito join a guild because he just so happened to save them. Episode 4 had him help a girl bring her pet back to life. Episodes 5-6 had him solving a murder. They were enjoyable to watch, and they did a good job at exploring the world within the MMO setting (introducing guilds dedicated to murdering people, duel system in towns, events only happening on certain days which people will do their best to complete).

It isn't without flaw though. I would have rather they spread out these episodes across the entirety of the Aincrad arc. The show basically jumps 1.5 years (or something like that, I don't know) within the space of 4 episodes. The main group trying to beat the game has gotten over halfway through the game by this point and we haven't seen any of that. One big problem that these six episodes had was pacing. I'd like to see what would have happened in those 1.5 years. To see the story split it's time between the main group doing their best to beat the game, and Kirito exploring Aincrad and observing the different stories going on, somewhat like Mushishi.
